newsitem.title: FRANCE: French consumer spending falls 0.8 pct in December.
newsitem.headline: French consumer spending falls 0.8 pct in December.

text.p: French consumer spending on manufactured goods slid 0.8 percent in December, producing a 3.4-percent fall over the fourth quarter of last year, national statistics institute INSEE said on Thursday.
December's drop, which followed a 0.5-percent fall in November, highlighted the weakness of the economy at the end of last year, economists said.
They said a variety of factors including cold winter weather and a late start to winter sales may have contributed to the slower pace of spending.
The data was weaker than many economists expected.

"(The data) confirms that consumer spending in the fourth quarter was pretty weak and that consumer spending's contribution to fourth-quarter gross domestic product will be negative," Deutsche Bank economist Patrick Mange said.
"On the other hand we are expecting a rebound in January, which will be partly due to sales that began on January 3 this year and that plays an important role."
